book.title: Cyber: Security Engineering in Rust
book.introduction: A security-engineering curriculum for learning Rust: understanding vulnerability classes and how Rust's ownership model prevents them, low-level and unsafe programming, cryptography, hardening, and defensive analysis (reverse engineering, malware analysis, and detection). The material is oriented toward building secure systems and understanding attacks in order to defend against them.

sections.title: How Ownership Prevents Use-After-Free
sections.description: Why use-after-free and double-free bugs are impossible in safe Rust, illustrated with C examples and their Rust equivalents.

sections.title: Buffer Overflows and Bounds Checking
sections.description: How out-of-bounds access causes memory corruption in C, and how Rust's bounds checking and slices prevent it.

sections.title: Integer Overflow and Wrapping Arithmetic
sections.description: Integer overflow as a vulnerability source; checked, wrapping, and saturating arithmetic in Rust.

sections.title: Data Races and the Send/Sync Traits
sections.description: How the type system prevents data races at compile time, and what that means for concurrent security-critical code.

sections.title: Uninitialized Memory and MaybeUninit
sections.description: Why reading uninitialized memory is undefined behavior, and how to work with it soundly.

sections.title: Raw Pointers and the unsafe Keyword
sections.description: What unsafe actually permits, and the invariants you must uphold when dereferencing raw pointers.

sections.title: Foreign Function Interface (FFI) with C
sections.description: Calling C libraries and exposing Rust to C safely; the security pitfalls at the boundary.

sections.title: Making Raw Syscalls
sections.description: Invoking operating-system syscalls directly, and why higher-level wrappers are safer.

sections.title: Memory Layout, repr(C), and Alignment
sections.description: Controlling struct layout for interoperability and safe parsing of binary formats.

sections.title: Auditing unsafe Code for Soundness
sections.description: How to review unsafe blocks, encapsulate them behind safe APIs, and use tools like Miri.

sections.title: Hashing and Message Authentication
sections.description: Cryptographic hashes and HMAC with the RustCrypto crates; where each is appropriate.

sections.title: Password Storage with Argon2
sections.description: Salting and using memory-hard password hashing correctly.

sections.title: Authenticated Symmetric Encryption (AEAD)
sections.description: Encrypting data with AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 and handling nonces safely.

sections.title: Public-Key Cryptography and Signatures
sections.description: Key exchange and digital signatures with ed25519 and x25519.

sections.title: Constant-Time Comparison and Side Channels
sections.description: Why naive comparisons leak secrets by timing, and how to avoid it.

sections.title: TLS with rustls
sections.description: Establishing encrypted connections and validating certificates correctly.

sections.title: Input Validation and Parsing Untrusted Data
sections.description: Parsing defensively so malformed input cannot cause panics or resource exhaustion.

sections.title: Handling Secrets in Memory (zeroize)
sections.description: Keeping keys and passwords out of logs and wiping them from memory after use.

sections.title: Avoiding Panics and Denial of Service
sections.description: Turning recoverable errors into Results and bounding memory and CPU use.

sections.title: Supply-Chain Security with cargo-audit and cargo-vet
sections.description: Auditing dependencies for known vulnerabilities and vetting third-party crates.

sections.title: Privilege Separation and Sandboxing
sections.description: Dropping privileges and confining a process with OS sandboxing primitives.

sections.title: Parsing ELF and PE Executables
sections.description: Reading executable headers and sections with the goblin crate for static analysis.

sections.title: Disassembly with Capstone
sections.description: Turning machine code back into assembly to understand a binary's behavior.

sections.title: Building a Hex Dump and Binary Inspector
sections.description: A command-line tool for examining raw file contents and extracting strings.

sections.title: Extracting Indicators of Compromise from Files
sections.description: Scanning binaries for URLs, IPs, and known signatures to support triage.

sections.title: Signature Scanning with YARA Rules
sections.description: Matching files against detection rules to classify known malware families.

sections.title: File Hashing and Reputation Lookups
sections.description: Computing sample hashes and checking them against threat-intelligence feeds.

sections.title: Entropy Analysis to Detect Packing
sections.description: Measuring byte entropy to flag encrypted or packed sections in a binary.

sections.title: Building a File-Integrity Monitor
sections.description: Watching the filesystem and alerting on unexpected changes to critical files.

sections.title: Log Parsing and Anomaly Detection
sections.description: Ingesting system logs and flagging suspicious patterns for a SOC workflow.

sections.title: Parsing Network Packets
sections.description: Decoding Ethernet, IP, and TCP/UDP headers from captured traffic.

sections.title: Building a TCP Port Scanner
sections.description: Asynchronously probing open ports to inventory a host you are authorized to test.

sections.title: A Simple Intrusion-Detection Sensor
sections.description: Matching traffic against rules and raising alerts on suspicious flows.

sections.title: Rate Limiting and Abuse Prevention
sections.description: Protecting a network service from floods and brute-force attempts.

sections.title: Session Tokens and JWTs
sections.description: Issuing and verifying signed tokens without introducing common flaws.

sections.title: Time-Based One-Time Passwords (TOTP)
sections.description: Implementing a standards-compliant second factor.

sections.title: Role-Based Access Control
sections.description: Modeling permissions in the type system so unauthorized actions do not compile.
